overall_reason: A deliberate Swiss red-black-white treatment with one giant number and directly labelled, proportional bars; the style is chosen, not defaulted, but the slide repeats its lead figure three times, leaves a dead middle band and makes claims its own data does not support.

findings.where: left column key message and top bar
findings.evidence: 'First open-source model to achieve SOTA across all three major coding benchmarks' but the first benchmark is labelled 'AIME 2025 / Mathematical Reasoning', not coding; '#1 OPEN-SOURCE RANKING' is shown while the chart compares only against closed models (Claude 3.5, GPT-4o), so no open-source rival is on the slide. Source line is 'Benchmark data sourced from official evaluation reports, 2025' with no report named. Failed T-THREE-LINE (not falsifiable as stated).
findings.before: "across all three major coding benchmarks"; '#1 OPEN-SOURCE RANKING'
findings.after: "Leads Claude 3.5 and GPT-4o on AIME 2025, SWE-bench Verified and τ²-bench" and a footnote naming each report and date [DATA NEEDED: report citations; open-source comparison set if '#1' is kept]
findings.why: A benchmark slide is only as good as the claims it can back; mislabelled categories and an unshown ranking read as invented proof.

findings.where: '95.7' in the left hero, the AIME column number, and the GLM-4.7 AIME bar
findings.evidence: T-DELETION: the 200px '95.7' hero and the 80px '95.7' AIME column header can each be removed without losing a fact; the same figure appears three times within 900px. The left hero also picks AIME, the one non-coding benchmark, as the lead number on a 'coding performance' slide. The columns then repeat 'big number + bar chart' three times, the stock data-slide shape SLD-136 warns against.
findings.after: Make the hero the slide's argument (e.g. '+20.5 on SWE-bench Verified', the largest coding margin) and keep each benchmark's score once, on its bar
findings.why: Repeating one number as decoration crowds out the point the slide should make.

findings.evidence: Between the '+x VS CLOSED-SOURCE BEST' lines and the summary row sits a ~290px empty band across all three benchmark columns (tile 1920-00); the left column is empty from y 560 to the footer.
findings.before: Bars top-aligned, summary pinned to bottom, empty middle
findings.after: Move the summary row up under the bars or enlarge the bars to use the height
findings.why: A dead band in the middle of a slide reads as a layout nobody finished.

findings.where: top bar, column heads and labels: 'BENCHMARK REPORT / 2025 CODING PERFORMANCE', 'OPEN-SOURCE SOTA' (x3), 'OPEN-SOURCE MODEL', 'AIME 2025 SCORE', 'BENCHMARKS WON'
findings.evidence: About 30 tracked-caps labels; 'OPEN-SOURCE SOTA' appears in the top-right, bottom-right and (as 'OPEN SOURCE') in the outline badge. T-LABEL-TRANSFORM: the badge and the second 'OPEN-SOURCE SOTA' lose nothing when removed.
findings.before: OPEN-SOURCE SOTA in top bar, footer and badge
findings.after: Keep one instance (top bar); delete the badge and the footer repeat
findings.why: Repeated caps labels are chrome, not information.

findings.evidence: The only title is the label 'BENCHMARK REPORT / 2025 CODING PERFORMANCE'; the assertion lives in 16px grey body text. Read as a ghost deck, the slide says 'benchmark report', not what was found.
findings.after: An assertion title: 'GLM-4.7 leads closed models on all three benchmarks' (if the claim survives the fix above)
findings.why: Slide titles should carry the argument.

strengths: Bars are drawn to scale, directly labelled and sorted, with the subject in red, the main rival in black and the rest in grey: a clear, intentional encoding.
The type-and-grid treatment (heavy grotesk numerals, hairline column rules, black top and bottom bars) is a chosen Swiss style executed consistently; do not soften it into cards.
not_investigated: Benchmark figures themselves were not fact-checked against external reports.
Only one slide captured; deck-level narrative (T-GHOST-DECK across slides) not possible.
